query: What signals indicate a hardware incident is in the anomaly window?

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: The reported symptom (connection_failure, disk_failure, overheating, physical_damage, etc.) is an observable characteristic of the incident that lies outside the anomaly-window label and plausibly carries strong signal about whether a hardware anomaly is present. It is not a deterministic restatement of the focus.

per_column.name: incident_scope_context
per_column.rationale: The scope of impact (single_workstation vs. server_infrastructure vs. network_segment) is a distinct contextual variable that can correlate with hardware-anomaly incidents without restating or leaking the label.

per_column.name: technician_assignment_stability
per_column.rationale: Whether the technician assignment stayed stable is derivable from routing behavior and is independent of the hardware-anomaly label; it may carry weak-to-moderate predictive signal (e.g., churn on ambiguous hardware cases). Legitimate predictor, though modest.

per_column.name: caller_repeat_status
per_column.rationale: Whether the caller is first-time vs. repeat/frequent is a behavioral attribute outside the focus. Repeated callers can be associated with recurring hardware faults, so it plausibly carries predictive signal without leakage.

per_column.name: software_update_interference
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag for whether a software update was involved is an external causal-context variable; it helps discriminate software- vs. hardware-driven incidents and does not restate or leak the hardware-anomaly label.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are legitimate predictors: each lies outside the focus variable, none is a deterministic function of or a post-outcome leak of the anomaly-window label, and each plausibly carries signal for distinguishing hardware-anomaly incidents. The strongest is failure_symptom, which directly characterizes the fault type, complemented by scope, software-update context, and caller/technician behavior. As a set they provide meaningful predictive leverage beyond the original administrative/metadata columns, though several features (technician stability, caller status) contribute only weak signal and high NULL rates in some columns limit coverage, so the aggregate utility is moderate rather than high.
